perf.summary: i*n is recomputed every inner iteration; hoist the row base pointer to remove a multiply from the inner loop and shorten the address dependency chain.
perf.currentCost: Inner loop indexes mat[i*n + j], recomputing i*n (a multiply) on each of the n*n iterations across both overloads.
perf.proposedChange: Before the inner loop: int* row = mat + i * n; (or long*) then sum += (long)row[j] * vec[j];. The compiler may already strength-reduce this, but the explicit row pointer guarantees a single add-stride access pattern Burst vectorizes cleanly.
perf.rationale: Replaces an inner-loop multiply with a hoisted base-plus-stride pointer, improving the chance Burst emits a contiguous SIMD load over row[j]. Same applies to both int* and long* overloads.
perf.risk: None. Pure index reassociation; identical results for all inputs.

perf.summary: Three stackalloc long[n] buffers are allocated on every PerformCheck call (once per Freivalds iteration); the br/cr intermediate buffers can be reused and the allocation hoisted out of the iters loop.
perf.currentCost: Per iteration: 3*n*8 bytes of fresh stack frame setup. Across iters iterations this re-stack-allocates repeatedly. cr is only needed transiently for the final compare.
perf.proposedChange: Allocate ar/br/cr once in Verify (outside the it-loop) and pass them in, reusing across iterations. Additionally, fold the c*r==a*(b*r) compare to avoid materializing cr fully: compute cr[i] inline and compare against ar[i] in one fused pass, dropping one buffer (2*n*8 bytes instead of 3).
perf.rationale: Hoisting stackalloc out of the loop removes repeated frame adjustment; fusing the final MatrixVectorMultiply(c) with the comparison eliminates the cr buffer and one full pass over results, cutting working set by a third and saving n stores+loads.
perf.risk: stackalloc inside a loop is technically reused frame space in C#, so RAM may already be constant; the real win is the fused c-multiply/compare dropping a buffer and a pass. Behavior identical: ar[i] != (c row . r) is the same test as ar[i] != cr[i].

perf.summary: r[i] = (int)((*seed & 1) * 2 - 1) repeatedly dereferences seed and uses a multiply; load seed into a local register for the whole loop and use a branchless bit-to-sign.
perf.currentCost: Each iteration reloads *seed (pointer dereference, no register caching across the xorshift) and computes a multiply-subtract to map {0,1}->{-1,1}.
perf.proposedChange: uint s = *seed; inside loop update s with the xorshift, write r[i] = (int)((s & 1u) << 1) - 1; and store *seed = s; once after the loop. The <<1 replaces the *2.
perf.rationale: Caching seed in a local removes a pointer round-trip per iteration and enables register allocation of the xorshift state; <<1 is a strength reduction of *2. Shortens the per-element dependency chain.
perf.risk: None. (s&1)<<1 - 1 yields exactly -1/1 as before. Writing seed back once preserves the same final RNG state, so subsequent iterations are identical.
